Discover Brilliance
Millfield is one of the leading UK independent schools for boys and girls, aged 2-18 years. Millfield is not like other schools and never has been. We believe in shaping the school around the child, where excellence in teaching and coaching comes together with the child at the centre. Our aim is that each individual will discover their own brilliance.
16 - 18 yrs Sixth Form
Millfield and Millfield Prep are distinctively different. We encourage our children and young adults to be kind, to challenge, to question, to be positive influencers and to have a voice. Our aim is that each individual will discover their own brilliance. We have the resource, the attitude and the capacity to lead the way and define education in the UK, now and in the future.
Gavin Horgan and Dan Thornburn - Millfield Headmaster and Millfield Prep Headmaster

About Us
Millfield Pre-Prep is located next to Millfield Prep, set in 200 acres of beautiful fields and woodland near Glastonbury. From day one children are welcomed into our community, nurtured and encouraged to reach their potential. Our experienced teachers work with small class sizes, in year group sets. We offer a broad range of subjects and activities, with spacious classrooms and a strong emphasis on outdoor learning. Our school values of Be Curious, Be You, Be Kind, Be Challengers and Be Brilliant shape our friendly and inclusive community.
We are fortunate to share excellent facilities with the Prep School, including a 25m heated indoor pool and tennis courts. Our pupils also benefit from the expertise of Millfield Prep coaches for sporting and creative activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: English as an Additional Language  at Millfield Prep School
pageCache.text:
English as an Additional Language
Leading EAL Programme in a UK Prep School
At Millfield Prep, we offer a leading EAL (English as an Additional Language) programme in the UK, designed to help international pupils thrive academically and socially. With strong pastoral care, expert teaching, and a fully immersive English-learning environment, pupils quickly gain confidence and fluency.
We provide a welcoming, inclusive and diverse boarding school experience, where pupils from around the world feel supported from their very first day.
Why Choose Millfield Prep for EAL?
Leading EAL programme in the UK
Strong pastoral care and student support
Cambridge English exam preparation
Immersive English-learning environment
Diverse and inclusive boarding school community
Wide range of extracurricular opportunities
An Immersive and Inclusive Learning Experience
Our approach ensures that pupils are fully integrated into school life while receiving the language support they need. We do not separate international pupils from their peers—instead, we create an immersive English-speaking environment where learning happens naturally every day.
Boarding pupils live alongside classmates from the UK and across the globe, building friendships and developing their English through real-life interaction. This international and inclusive community helps pupils settle quickly and feel at home.
Personalised EAL Support and Cambridge Exam Preparation
Our EAL programme is tailored to each individual. Lessons are taught in small groups by experienced specialists who identify and respond to each pupil’s needs.
Pupils typically receive between six and sixteen EAL lessons per week, while spending most of their time in mainstream classes. This balance allows them to develop language skills while fully participating in the curriculum.
We also support pupils with Cambridge English exam preparation, helping them achieve internationally recognised qualifications and preparing them for future academic success.
Through engaging lessons focused on speaking, listening, reading, and writing, pupils gain the confidence to express themselves clearly and succeed across all subjects.
Strong Pastoral Care for International Pupils
We understand that moving to a new country is a big step. Our strong pastoral care system ensures that every pupil feels safe, supported, and valued.
Staff work closely with pupils to support both their academic progress and emotional wellbeing, helping them adapt to life in a UK boarding school with confidence.
A Diverse Boarding School Community
Millfield Prep is proud to be a diverse and inclusive international school. Pupils benefit from learning in a multicultural environment that celebrates different perspectives and cultures.
Throughout the year, we mark global festivals such as Chinese New Year and Christmas, helping pupils feel connected to both their home culture and their new environment.
Enriching Activities Beyond the Classroom
Our pupils enjoy a wide range of extracurricular activities, including horse riding, sailing, fencing, orchestra, archery, and chess. These activities support language development, confidence, and teamwork.
Educational trips throughout the year allow pupils to experience life in Britain and practise their English in real-world settings.
A highlight of the year is our International Evening, where pupils share food, music, and traditions from around the world—celebrating the diversity of our school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior Department - At Millfield Prep School in Glastonbury
pageCache.text:
Junior Department
Pupils aged 7-10 (Years 3-5) in the Junior Department study in small classes and are taught by primary-trained teachers for many of their subjects. From Years 3 to 5, pupils are set in Maths according to ability, thereby allowing for differentiation to challenge and support pupils appropriately. In Year 6, pupils are also set for Maths and are taught by specialist teachers in each subject.
Classes are headed by a group tutor who is responsible for a pupil’s general programme and welfare; they also teach many of the lessons in Years 3-5. We believe it is essential that all pupils acquire a good grasp of English and Maths, and the Junior staff also teach Science, Humanities and Art. Other subjects, such as Design & Technology, ICT, Languages, Music, Drama and PE, are taught by subject specialists who are experienced in teaching primary-aged pupils.
The Junior Department follows the International Primary Curriculum (IPC). IPC is a thematic, inquiry-based curriculum that provides a clear process of learning along with specific learning goals for every subject. It provides the children with an exciting, enriched, challenging and extensive learning journey, which focuses not just on the UK but also on modern-day issues across the globe, whilst at the same time encompassing the British national curriculum.
Juniors enjoy regular trips and experience days, which enhance their learning around specific units of work. They relish opportunities to take their learning outdoors, either to local places and habitats of interest or out in the school’s grounds.

Facilities
At Millfield Pre-Prep, healthy living and being active is at the heart of our philosophy. We have world-class facilities, expert Millfield coaches and offer weekly swimming lessons in our on-site pool.
We believe that enjoyment and participation in a variety of sport not only provides an education in its own right, but instils in children a healthy approach to life and learning.
Each week, all children from age two upwards benefit from swimming lessons in our 25m heated indoor pool, as well as having PE and Games sessions, which include dance, gymnastics and ball skills.
There are over 20 free after-school clubs to take part in at Millfield Pre-Prep including pottery, chess, cricket, gymnastics, cookery, gardening, computer skills and jewellery making.
Our setting includes Apple Green, an Assembly Hall, Pre-Prep Dining Hall, soft playground area, walled garden, Forest School, IT suite and classrooms specially equipped for each year group.

Younger children are served directly at the tables by their teachers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum - At Millfield Prep School in Glastonbury
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Junior Department Years 3-6
Pupils aged 7-11 (Years 3-6) work for the majority of their time in the Junior Department. The pupils study in small classes, headed by a group tutor who is responsible for their pupils' general programme and welfare; they also teach many of the lessons. We believe it is essential that all pupils acquire a good grasp of English and Maths and the Junior staff also teach Science, Humanities and Art through the inquiry-based International Primary Curriculum (IPC).
The IPC develops pupils' knowledge, skills and understanding through engaging, thematic learning. Each unit is carefully structured around clear learning goals and encourages children to make meaningful connections across subjects while developing an international perspective.
Throughout their learning, pupils are supported in developing the eight IPC Personal Goals: adaptability, communication, cooperation, empathy, resilience, respect, thoughtfulness and morality. Through enquiry-based activities, collaboration, reflection and problem-solving, pupils are encouraged to become confident, independent learners who can apply their knowledge in a range of contexts.
Regular opportunities for assessment and feedback help to celebrate progress, identify next steps and ensure every child is supported to achieve their full potential. The IPC provides a rich and engaging learning experience that inspires curiosity, creativity and a lifelong love of learning.
Other subjects such as DT, ICT, Languages, Music, Drama and PE are taught by subject specialists who are experienced in teaching primary aged pupils. In Year 6, pupils are taught by specialist teachers and some class-based tutors.
Years 6-8
In Years 6-8, your child will be taught by some further specialist subject teachers and class-based tutors. The programme will continue to be overseen by their group tutor, who will also keep a close and friendly eye on how your child is developing outside the classroom – in Sport, Music and other activities. English and Maths are still central to the curriculum. Pupils also study Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Humanities, Religious Studies, Art, Food Technology, Design and Technology, Computing & ICT, Music, Drama and PE. Language options include French, Spanish and Latin.
Years 7-8
Brilliance Curriculum
Millfield and Millfield Prep established the aspirational Brilliance Curriculum, developed in recent years to form cross-curricular links between subjects and topics from Year 7 to Year 13, to aid greater understanding. Carefully curated curriculum maps plot the learning journey to maximise knowledge layering, interlinking similar concepts across topics and the order they are taught in.
Pre-Senior Baccalaureate
Millfield Prep have adopted the Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB) to run alongside the Brilliance Curriculum in Years 7 & 8. This is a programme of study that aims to prepare children for the challenges of life as young adults in senior schools. The PSB is designed to help pupils develop a wide range of core skills including Independence; Communication; Collaboration; Thinking and Learning; Leadership; and Reviewing and Improving.
The PSB focuses on life-long skills that:
· Develop flexible and adaptable intelligence
· Bridge the gap previously lacking in a content-based curriculum
· Foster application in the individual
· Promote excellent communicators
· Challenge pupils’ perceptions of school
· Inspire a love of learning
· Ensure collaboration and teamwork are at the core
The PSB allows pupils to celebrate their differences and increases opportunities to demonstrate their learning in varied ways in addition to written tests. Examples include writing extended individual or group projects; design projects; completing practical work; making artefacts; performing on stage or on the sports pitches; and presenting work orally.
“Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once he grows up." - Pablo Picasso
We believe every child is an artist and our aim is to build confidence through creative play and visual self-expression, so as to allow their potential to flourish.
Drawing underpins everything we do and is the skeleton onto which we build any body of work. An expansive range of skills and techniques are taught, which are used to develop imagination and independent creative thinking.
We are very fortunate to have fantastic facilities and to be surrounded by such inspiring natural beauty. Pupils experience and are taught the full range of both 2D and 3D processes. We have a well-equipped pottery studio and a purpose-built carving area, where pupils are taught to carve in stone.
The department is a hive of activity throughout the week, as well as weekends, with a full range of clubs and activities for all ages. Art trips are organised across the age ranges, that offer excellent learning experiences beyond the classroom.
Every pupil has the opportunity of exhibiting their work around the school and each week one piece of art is highlighted and becomes the ‘Picture of the Week’.
Creative Arts at Millfield Prep
Find out more about Art Scholarships
Whatever pupils go on to do in the future, IT skills will most probably be essential, as everyone is now expected to have sound digital skills.
Pupils are taught the following skills during their time at Millfield Prep:
· Desktop Publishing
· Graphical Representation of Data
· Online Communications
· Presentations Graphics
· Monitoring & Control
· Programming/Game Creation
In Years 3 and 4, pupils begin to learn the basics, including sending emails, using different fonts, search engines, creating and using databases, cutting and pasting text, creating pie charts and graphs, interpreting and analysing information in graphs and simple programming & coding using Scratch, the Dash & Dot robots and Lego Spike Essential. In Year 5, they begin to use spreadsheets and sensors, collect and interpret data, use an iPad to take pictures and edit the images using Adobe Express. On top of this, they create interactive presentations/storybooks using Purple Mash and develop their programming and coding skills further through game creation in Scratch, and by using Lego Spike Essential and Sphero robots. In Year 6, pupils look at creating various graphs in some detail, as well as becoming familiar with Microsoft Office 365 and its inbuilt tools to support their learning across the curriculum. They go on to design a poster, learn more skills with a digital camera, create a slideshow and are introduced to simple video editing.
In Year 7, pupils look at digital imagery using Adobe Express and Canva, further develop their knowledge of spreadsheets, create a presentation, learn how to perform further programming functions using a BBC Microbit and Lego Spike Prime, and become more familiar with Microsoft Office 365. In Year 8, pupils develop many of the skills learnt over the previous years, including Canva, Excel and Word, as well as being introduced to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and further developing their programming skills via a Raspberry Pi and the Python programming language.
Incredible facilities at your fingertips
We have three purpose-built computer labs, each containing networked PCs running Windows 11. Each lab also has a colour laser printer, an interactive panel and a second large digital display screen.
As part of our Mobile Learning Project, our Junior Department has a supply of iPads, that are used in both ICT and subject teaching. For pupils in Years 6, 7 and 8, it is compulsory for them to purchase an iPad through our educational partner. This device is fully managed by the school to allow greater online safety/security and reduce online distractions during teaching and learning time.
Design & Technology at Millfield Prep is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject.
Using creativity and imagination, pupils design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values. In doing so, they acquire a broad range of subject knowledge and draw on disciplines such as mathematics, science, engineering, computing and art. Through the evaluation of past and present design and technology, they also develop a critical understanding of its impact on daily life and the wider world.
Design & Technology is taught to Years 3 and 4 on a weekly basis throughout the academic year in the technology workshops. From Year 5 upwards, pupils learn Design & Technology for two terms and Food Technology for one term each year, working on a rotation carousel. After school clubs are available for all ages, as we look to provide opportunities for all those interested. This subject is growing at Millfield Prep, with Year 9 Design and Innovation Scholarships available at Millfield Senior and success being gained by the Year 6 Kit Car Club at the external Goblin Kit Car regional competition.
Coming up this year:
Every pupil at Millfield Prep School has the opportunity to benefit from both weekly Drama classes and highly-anticipated whole-year productions. We find that these classes help not only those who wish to better their acting skills or perform on stage, but that the benefits of these lessons extend far beyond the drama studio.
We asked the Drama department all about the benefits that drama classes and performance opportunities bring to our pupils.
"Drama is life with the dull bits cut out." - Alfred Hitchcock
Drama is available to every pupil at Millfield Prep and is part of the curriculum. Pupils are encouraged to find ways to express themselves, develop greater confidence, work in a team and share the ‘limelight’, fostering a love of film and stage that can be enjoyed for a lifetime.
All pupils have the opportunity to perform to an audience, be it their peers or the whole school. Each year group has a production, and if a child auditions and is willing to devote time and energy, then they will not be turned away. Auditions are used solely to assign roles. Recent productions have had casts of over 60 children, all with speaking roles.
Productions including:
For those who enjoy the technical side of theatre, there are also opportunities to play a part. One of our ex-pupils who managed lighting and effects in several shows is now Production Manager for The Lion King.
In tandem with studying Drama, we incorporate Media Studies and introduce topics such as Audience, Genre, Narrative, Marketing and Symbolism. We have recently introduced a portable TV studio, where pupils can learn to produce, edit and manage sound and lighting for film productions. They can also create music videos and DVDs.
Pupils can also choose to take LAMDA exams and participate in Speech & Drama as a co-curricular club.
Millfield Prep's Drama lessons lead to many pupils becoming involved. Parents have been amazed at the positive effect of school drama on their children
The Good Schools Guide
Creative Arts at Millfield Prep
‘A word after a word after a word is power’ – Margaret Atwood
Our goal is to open up the world to children through understanding the power of words and the importance of how communication enriches their lives. Having something to say and knowing how best to articulate those ideas is what we want for our pupils. We believe that learning new ideas through reading and relaxing with a book are essential life skills, especially in a fast-paced digital world where children need the space to slow down, imagine, and build critical thinking skills as well as strengthen their comprehension, empathy, and resilience. Being confident to speak and present ideas, and developing the skills to listen, understand and communicate are increasingly important. We work very closely with our PCC department to ensure that all children are able to access the English curriculum at their level of understanding. Our aim is that children leave us with a love of reading, writing and a confidence in communicating.
To foster their love of literature and develop the skills they will require in the Senior School, we teach an engaging mix of English topics: thematic poetry from a range of voices and time periods; a creative introduction to fundamental literary genres; an interactive study of Shakespeare; exploration of the power of language; and crafting interesting and original narratives. The emphasis within these final years at the Prep is very much to instil a passion and genuine love for English which we hope will remain within them throughout their lives.
We have a welcoming, comfortable library for pupils in Years 1–8 to read, research, and enjoy books. It offers a range of seating areas so children can settle with a book or work quietly, and it is open throughout the school day, including breaks, lunch and after school. The library is run by an experienced librarian who supports pupils in choosing books, building reading confidence, and developing their information-finding skills during their fortnightly library visits. Our collection is updated regularly with new titles, and pupils are encouraged to request books they would like added. We also hold a wide range of dyslexia-friendly books and accessible formats to ensure every pupil can find something that suits them. In reading lessons, children have the time to read independently and to check in with their teacher to discuss the books they are reading.
Every year, pupils take part in national celebrations of literature. World Book Day and National Poetry Day are just a few of the events that pupils engage in, which can involve dressing up, hearing visiting writers speak, taking part in creative workshops, and joining in themed activities and competitions to help ignite and fuel their passion for English and reading. Our library also serves as the base for workshops during our author and poet visits, giving pupils the chance to learn directly from writers.
We also offer pupils the opportunity to take part in the Carnegie Medal

Millfield Prep School is an extraordinary place that provides boarding and day children with exceptional, unparalleled opportunities. With academic rigour, specialist sporting programmes and co-curricular excellence delivered in harmony, whatever their passions may be our pupils find something to fully immerse themselves in.
Not only is every child seen and known as an individual, but Millfield also firmly believes that every child is brilliant – and it is our mission to help them discover their brilliance and then nurture it to the full.
Outstanding pastoral care is at the core of everything. Kindness and consideration of others is central to all that we are and all that we do. Happy children thrive and succeed; and Millfield is full of success stories!
Dan Thornburn - Millfield Prep Headmaster
